knowledge:
- key_parameters: infoFile=Path to the formatted PPI data file ;; proteinList=Character vector of protein identifiers (e.g., UniProt IDs) to find paths between ;; outFolder=Directory path where the HTML visualization files will be written ;; maxPathLength=Maximum number of steps allowed in the identified paths (default is 2)
- alternatives: RCy3=Use when you want to visualize networks in the Cytoscape desktop application instead of a web browser ;; STRINGdb=Use for direct functional enrichment and network plotting of STRING database interactions without local HTML generation
- when_to_use: Use when you have a list of candidate proteins (e.g., from proteomics) and want to identify and interactively explore the shortest physical or signaling interaction paths connecting them.
- pitfalls: Mismatched protein identifier types (e.g., mixing Gene Symbols with UniProt IDs) will result in zero paths found ;; Large protein lists can generate massive HTML files that cause web browsers to freeze or lag.

workflows.name: ppi_path_visualization
workflows.intent: Identify shortest interaction paths among a set of proteins and generate an interactive HTML visualization.
input: protein_list.txt (a text file containing protein identifiers, one per line)
ppi_data.tsv (protein-protein interaction data downloaded from BioGRID or STRING)
workflows.stages: 1. Format the raw PPI data into the required format using format_ppi ;; 2. Run the path-finding algorithm and generate the HTML visualization using cisPath
workflows.code:
library(cisPath)
infoFile <- format_ppi(interaction_file, source="STRING", species="9606")
proteinList <- c("P01112", "Q01844", "P01116", "P01111")
cisPath(infoFile, proteinList, outFolder=tempdir())
